title: XAUDIT — x-brief-auditor output
description: Findings from auditing one step's BRIEF against the outputs it produced. Every finding names the instruction that failed, a real output that demonstrates it, the cause, and the exact replacement text. The shape is enforced here; the rules a schema cannot express (evidence must be real, replacement text must be specific, findings must be ordered) are enforced by code/checks/XAUDIT.py.

step.description: The step code audited, e.g. ECAT. Must equal the input's `step`.

findings.description: One entry per instruction that failed, ordered by outputs_affected, descending. May be empty — finding nothing is a valid answer and is better than inventing one.

id.description: F1, F2, … in the same order as the array.

cause.description: instruction_was_correct is a real verdict: the instruction was right, clear and checkable, and the fault lies with the agent or the source.

fix_in.description: If a script could detect the failure, this is `check` — never `brief`. A prompt rule nobody enforces is a wish.

instruction_quoted.description: The failing passage, copied from the brief character for character. Where the failure is an ABSENT instruction, quote the nearest passage that should have carried it and set instruction_absent true.

instruction_absent.description: True when the finding is that no instruction covers this at all; instruction_quoted then holds the passage where it belongs.

evidence.description: Real outputs that demonstrate the failure. An imagined example is not evidence.

field.description: Dotted path into the output, e.g. traps[0].label

value.description: The value actually produced, copied exactly.

replacement_text.description: The words that go in the file — not a description of a change. For a deletion, say so and quote what is removed.

outputs_affected.description: How many outputs the fix would change. Counted, never estimated. This is the ranking key.

working.description: Instructions checked and found sound. Not politeness: it stops the next person rewriting a constraint that was holding the output together, and it records what was actually looked at.
